entries.name: square-of-the-pawn
entries.definition: A square-control idea related to square of the pawn. Dominating key squares can restrict enemy pieces and create stable long-term pressure.

entries.name: stafford-gambit
entries.definition: An opening line in which material is offered for development, center control, or initiative. Success depends on active piece play, not on recovering material immediately.

entries.name: Stalemate
entries.definition: Side to move has no legal moves and is not in check, resulting in a draw.

entries.name: stalemate-avoidance
entries.definition: A conversion motif where the winning side avoids stalemate traps while preserving a forced win.

entries.name: standard
entries.definition: A strategic theme that rewards accurate evaluation: improve the least active piece, limit counterplay, and convert only when concrete tactics justify it.

entries.name: steinitz-attack
entries.definition: An attacking plan that builds pressure through piece coordination and open lines, then converts the initiative with forcing moves once calculation confirms it.

entries.name: structure
entries.definition: A pawn-structure idea involving structure. Time pawn breaks carefully, then place pieces to attack the weak squares and fixed targets that result.

entries.name: structure-damage
entries.definition: A pawn-structure idea involving structure damage. Time pawn breaks carefully, then place pieces to attack the weak squares and fixed targets that result.

entries.name: supported-mate
entries.definition: A checkmate where the mating piece is protected, preventing capture as a defense. Confirm support before committing.

entries.name: system-opening
entries.definition: A setup-based opening approach with flexible move order, where piece coordination and central control matter more than memorizing exact sequences.

entries.name: tactic
entries.definition: A concrete tactical motif around tactic. Calculate forcing moves first and verify whether the line wins material, initiative, or checkmate.

entries.name: tactical-shot
entries.definition: A concrete tactical motif around tactical shot. Calculate forcing moves first and verify whether the line wins material, initiative, or checkmate.

entries.name: tactics
entries.definition: A concrete tactical motif around tactics. Calculate forcing moves first and verify whether the line wins material, initiative, or checkmate.

entries.name: Tempo
entries.definition: A single move; gaining tempo means improving while forcing the opponent.

entries.name: Tempo Move
entries.definition: A move that improves your position while forcing a reply.

entries.name: tempo-gain-available
entries.definition: A developing move that simultaneously attacks an enemy piece, gaining time by forcing the opponent to respond defensively while you improve your position.

entries.name: tension
entries.definition: A position where opposing pieces or pawns attack each other and captures are possible, but neither side has committed. Keeping tension can preserve options and force mistakes; releasing it should be timed to win space, activity, or concrete tactics.

entries.name: the-spike
entries.definition: A strategic theme that rewards accurate evaluation: improve the least active piece, limit counterplay, and convert only when concrete tactics justify it.

entries.name: theory
entries.definition: An opening plan that emphasizes rapid development, king safety, and central influence, with tactics arising from improved piece activity.

entries.name: Threat
entries.definition: A move that creates a future danger the opponent must respect.

entries.name: torre-attack
entries.definition: An attacking plan that builds pressure through piece coordination and open lines, then converts the initiative with forcing moves once calculation confirms it.

entries.name: trade
entries.definition: A strategic exchange decision related to trade. Trade when it improves structure, piece quality, or king safety.

entries.name: trade-sequence
entries.definition: A strategic exchange decision related to trade sequence. Trade when it improves structure, piece quality, or king safety.

entries.name: transposition
entries.definition: A transposition reaches a familiar position through a different move order, so understanding structures and plans matters more than strict sequence.

entries.name: trap
entries.definition: A tactical trap that invites a natural-looking move and punishes it with a forcing sequence.

entries.name: trapped-piece
entries.definition: A piece with no safe escape squares. Restrict exits first, then win material with forcing play.

entries.name: trapped-piece-motif
entries.definition: A piece has no safe squares to retreat to and can be won by restricting its remaining escape routes and then capturing it.

entries.name: Triangulation
entries.definition: A maneuver to lose a tempo and transfer move obligation to the opponent.

entries.name: trick
entries.definition: A strategic theme that rewards accurate evaluation: improve the least active piece, limit counterplay, and convert only when concrete tactics justify it.

entries.name: trompowsky-attack
entries.definition: An attacking plan that builds pressure through piece coordination and open lines, then converts the initiative with forcing moves once calculation confirms it.

entries.name: Undefended pieces
entries.definition: Pieces with no friendly defender. Loose targets are often tactical entry points for forks, pins, and captures.

entries.name: under-defended-square
entries.definition: A critical square has fewer defenders than attackers, or could easily become loose, making it a target for piece invasion or tactical strikes.

entries.name: under-promotion
entries.definition: Promoting to a knight, rook, or bishop instead of a queen to force a precise tactical or mating result.

entries.name: Underpromotion
entries.definition: Promoting a pawn to a piece other than a queen for tactical reasons.

entries.name: undeveloped-piece-blocking
entries.definition: A piece remains on its starting square and blocks a rook from connecting or entering the game, reducing overall coordination and activity.

entries.name: unobstructed-diagonal-toward-king
entries.definition: A clear diagonal leads straight to the enemy king with no blocking pawns or pieces, giving bishops and queens direct attacking access.

entries.name: unpin
entries.definition: A tactic where a piece cannot move because it would expose a more valuable piece or critical square. Attack what the pinned piece is forced to defend.

entries.name: urussov-gambit
entries.definition: An opening line in which material is offered for development, center control, or initiative. Success depends on active piece play, not on recovering material immediately.

entries.name: very-long
entries.definition: A deep calculation category requiring long forcing lines and accurate move order. Practical success comes from candidate-move discipline.

entries.name: vienna-gambit
entries.definition: An opening line in which material is offered for development, center control, or initiative. Success depends on active piece play, not on recovering material immediately.

entries.name: vienna-game
entries.definition: An opening family where understanding development priorities, pawn structures, and recurring tactical motifs is more important than rote memorization.

entries.name: waiting
entries.definition: A waiting concept uses a useful pass move to preserve flexibility and provoke a concession in positions where tempo matters.

entries.name: waiting-move
entries.definition: A waiting concept uses a useful pass move to preserve flexibility and provoke a concession in positions where tempo matters.

entries.name: Weak Square
entries.definition: A square that cannot be controlled by pawns and can be occupied by pieces.

entries.name: Weak squares around king
entries.definition: Squares near the king that are attacked but not adequately defended, creating tactical access points.

entries.name: weak-entry-square
entries.definition: A square on an open file or rank where an enemy rook or queen can penetrate into the position with little resistance, often on the seventh or eighth rank.

entries.name: weak-king-squares
entries.definition: Dark or light squares around the king lack pawn protection, creating holes that enemy pieces can exploit for attacks or mating nets.

entries.name: weak-promotion-square
entries.definition: The queening square of a passed pawn is poorly defended, making it difficult to stop the pawn from promoting.

entries.name: Weakness
entries.definition: A target in the position such as a loose piece, weak pawn, or exposed king.

entries.name: white-setup
entries.definition: A strategic theme that rewards accurate evaluation: improve the least active piece, limit counterplay, and convert only when concrete tactics justify it.

entries.name: win-material
entries.definition: A tactical sequence aimed at winning or recovering material through forcing moves, often by deflecting, overloading, or pinning a key defender.

entries.name: winning-the-queen
entries.definition: A material recovery theme that uses forcing tactics to regain losses or convert tactical pressure into net material gain.

entries.name: X-Ray Attack
entries.definition: Pressure passes through a piece to attack a target behind it.

entries.name: x-ray-attack
entries.definition: Pressure that works through an intervening piece along a file, rank, or diagonal. If the front piece moves, the rear target is hit.

entries.name: x-ray-attack-motif
entries.definition: A piece exerts pressure through an intervening piece along a line. If the front piece moves or is captured, the rear target is hit.

entries.name: Zugzwang
entries.definition: Any legal move worsens the player's position.

entries.name: Zwischenzug
entries.definition: An in-between move is played before the expected move.
